identityFieldNote: caseData.docketNumber and caseData.countyName are the participant's own required screening answers and are deliberately left blank in the fixtures under the artifact convention. The rendered request cannot go out without them; they are supplied by the participant, never by LegalEase.
expectFailure: Must fail pleading QA. Every ground below is either a prohibited term for this component or prohibited invention. (1) Prohibited terms: the fixture uses 'petition', 'Petitioner', 'sealed' and 'destroyed'. The controlling scope restriction is that this relief is court-driven, requires no petition, and that anyone who completed a deferred sentence must not be sold a petition packet; 'sealed' is the chapter 230 remedy and § 7041 is chapter 221 expungement, which Act 60 did not amend; and no source says a § 7041(e) expungement destroys the file — chapter 230 file destruction is a different chapter. (2) It proceeds while restitution is outstanding. The statute provides that the record is not expunged until restitution has been paid in full; that is a statutory bar on the relief, not a document to be gathered, and a participant asking whether the record can be cleared anyway is an express self-help stop condition. (3) It proceeds on a registrable sex offence, which § 7041(h) subjects to a confidential VCIC special index that survives the expungement and which is an express self-help stop condition. (4) It asserts that no finding of good cause exists and predicts that the court will grant. Section 7041(e) makes the relief mandatory only absent a finding of good cause by the court; a good-cause signal is a self-help stop condition, and no court outcome may be predicted. (5) It asserts outside-party acts no source states: that the Restitution Unit confirmed a zero balance to LegalEase, that the clerk agreed the order was overlooked, and that VCIC has already updated its records. (6) It asserts service on the State's Attorney and a prosecutor position ('does not object') when the registry records service as none by the participant, no notice to a prosecutor, and § 7608 victim notice as not attaching to this chapter 221 relief. (7) It asserts a hearing outcome and a date, and promises the participant a clean background check — when expunged Vermont records may still appear in a federal criminal background check and Vermont relief does not reach federal records. (8) It states a filing fee and a fee waiver, when the registry records the fee as none and the fee waiver as not applicable because no fee is charged; stating either is an unsourced assertion about money. (9) It states an interval — 'the statutory thirty-day deadline for the order has passed' — when how long after discharge a Vermont court in practice enters the order is an open release blocker and no such deadline appears in any source. (10) It fills court identity no source supplies: court name, county, docket number, OTN, judge, prosecutor and filing date, none of which LegalEase may prefill. (11) It populates protected fields — date of birth, SSN last four, state ID, driver's licence, FBI number and a fingerprint identifier — which must stay blank; date of birth and docket number are themselves among the items § 7041(h) records in the confidential special index. (12) It states an eligibilityBasisLabel asserting confirmed eligibility when no eligibility conclusion may be asserted on this track.
